Main objective & specific objectives

Monitor locally.
Support earlier warning.

Design, develop, test and evaluate a low-cost, offline-capable neonatal monitor for local hypothermia and hypoxia warnings, with AI risk scoring and trend analysis when connected.

  1. Design: integrate sensors, display, alerts and timekeeping.
  2. Develop: connect firmware, API, database, AI and dashboard.
  3. Test: verify components and integrated dataflow.
  4. Evaluate: measure performance against a threshold-only baseline.

Proposal §1.3 · Report §§1.3–1.4, 7.3–7.6

01 · Problem statement

The gap between observation rounds.

The proposal identifies a need in rural Ugandan clinics for affordable, continuous monitoring of temperature, oxygen saturation and heart rate despite unreliable connectivity and power.

Intermittent checks can leave deterioration unnoticed. A useful system must warn at the bedside and preserve readings when connectivity fails.

Multiple vital signsOffline local alertsTraceable history

02 · Sensor: MAX30102

Light reads the pulse.

  • MAX30102 — heart rate and SpO₂ over I²C.

Red and infrared light shine into the fingertip, and the sensor reads how the returned light changes with every heartbeat.

02 · Sensor: MLX90614

Temperature without touching.

  • MLX90614 — non-contact temperature over the same bus.

The sensor estimates surface temperature from infrared energy. Clinical interpretation requires controlled distance, calibration and comparison with a reference thermometer.

02 · Objective 1 — Design hardware

One integrated sensing path.

  • Sense: MAX30102 + MLX90614 on I²C.
  • Record: ESP32-S3, DS1302 and microSD.
  • Respond: ST7789 display, RGB LED and buzzer.

Achieved at prototype integration level.

Recorded SPI-carrier checks: 0 ERC, 0 DRC, 0 unrouted and 0 schematic-parity violations.

Design revision: proposed LCD + DS3231 → implemented ST7789 + DS1302. Measurement accuracy and physical fit still require qualification.

Specific objective 1 · Achieved at prototype integration level

Design and integrate the hardware

Interface the sensing, display, alert and timekeeping hardware with the ESP32 to acquire vital-sign signals and support local monitoring.

How we achieved it

  1. Connected MAX30102 and MLX90614 on shared I²C: GPIO4 SDA and GPIO5 SCL. Their addresses, 0x57 and 0x5A, responded with zero bus errors.
  2. Connected DS1302 on GPIO6/7/14, ST7789 on GPIO8–12 and microSD on GPIO21/40/41/42. The implemented display/RTC replaced the proposed LCD/DS3231.
  3. Added local outputs: buzzer on GPIO15 and RGB on GPIO16/17/18. Display text/colour bars and command-driven buzzer beeps were observed.
  4. Produced the schematic and two-layer SPI carrier. Recorded ERC, DRC, unrouted and schematic-parity issues were all zero.

Recorded evidence

2 sensorsI²C devices responded at 0x57 and 0x5A
91,561–105,770MAX30102 infrared counts with finger; about 700 uncovered
25.97–30.73 °CObserved MLX90614 surface readings, not neonatal body temperatures
4 / 4SD diagnostic attempts passed

The numbers demonstrate that the hardware exchanged signals, acquired changing sensor data, displayed output and stored records. They do not establish calibrated measurement accuracy.

Remaining work: Finger-test heart-rate estimates ranged from 42 to 187 bpm without a reference instrument. The maximum surface-to-ambient difference was 0.84 °C, below the configured 1.5 °C warm-target condition, so no warm-target events were recorded. Battery endurance and clinical accuracy remain unverified.

Reviewed report §§7.3.2–7.3.6 · Recorded report results; synthetic AI figures are not clinical validation.

03 · Objective 2 — Develop firmware

Local alerts remain independent.

The ESP32 samples, validates and timestamps readings, applies local thresholds, then stores and synchronises data.

  • Abnormal reading: display, LED and buzzer respond locally.
  • No connection: buffer readings on microSD.
  • Connection restored: upload queued records.

Recorded runs: 588 / 230 saved rows; 0 sampler resets and 0 temperature-packet errors in both. Runtime, heartbeat and sync returned HTTP 200.

From readings to a shared view.

Flask + PostgreSQL store patients, devices, sessions, readings, alerts and risk scores.

Specific objective 2 · Achieved as a working prototype

Develop the connected software

Build firmware, a Flask/PostgreSQL backend and a React dashboard with local threshold alerts, offline buffering, synchronisation and explainable AI.

How we achieved it

  1. Firmware samples and validates readings, timestamps them and applies bedside threshold rules. Invalid or removed-sensor readings are marked unavailable rather than interpreted as normal.
  2. The local display, LED and buzzer do not wait for a network connection or AI response. microSD preserves queued records during connectivity loss.
  3. On reconnection, firmware sends JSON records to the Flask API. The backend authenticates the request and persists readings, sessions and alerts in PostgreSQL.
  4. The backend calculates advisory risk/trend information; React presents current and historical readings, alerts and explanations for a nurse to review.

Recorded evidence

588 / 230Rows saved in two analysed diagnostic runs
0 / 0Sampler resets / temperature-packet errors in both runs
HTTP 200Runtime, heartbeat and sync requests in both runs
120 s → 12Causal history window → AI features: last, mean, slope and variation for three vital signs

The recorded runs support working storage and device-to-backend communication. HTTP 200 indicates successful request handling; it does not prove clinical correctness or a guaranteed delivery time.

Remaining work: Saved-row counts are from different diagnostic runs, not an end-to-end loss-rate experiment. Controlled offline recovery, dashboard delay and production reliability were not fully quantified. AI is advisory and does not gate local alerts.

Reviewed report §§7.4.1–7.4.6 · Recorded report results; synthetic AI figures are not clinical validation.

05 · AI integration

AI sees the trend, not just the alarm.

The backend model looks at a causal 120-second history and, for temperature, SpO₂ and heart rate, calculates the last value, mean, slope and variation.

  • Features: 12 explainable time-series features.
  • Model: logistic regression with a validation-selected threshold of 0.75.
  • Output: risk score, contributing factors and trend flags.
  • Boundary: AI is advisory; local ESP32 alerts remain independent.
Specific objective 3 · Partly achieved

Test components and integrated dataflow

Test hardware, firmware, backend and dashboard individually and together, including connectivity, API behaviour and access control.

How we achieved it

  1. Compiled and uploaded firmware; verified the programmed flash hash. Scanned the sensor bus and exercised the display, buzzer, RGB and microSD.
  2. Tested SD write, read, append, compare and delete operations; repeated SD verification while RGB output states were active.
  3. Ran firmware tests for threshold alarms, temperature-packet validation, stale readings, finger removal and heart-rate averaging safeguards.
  4. Ran backend checks for authentication, access control, reading round-trip, quality-aware alerts, pagination, clock validation and synchronisation retry/rate-limit handling.

Recorded evidence

21 / 21Backend tests passed at the recorded checkpoint
4Database migrations applied to a fresh database
0Reported schema differences after migration
345,966 B / 24,912 BFlash / static RAM for the display-and-sensor diagnostic build

These results support functional integration, persistence and the tested access-control paths. Passing tests is not a clinical validation study or a complete security audit.

Remaining work: No verified reference-instrument accuracy dataset, controlled sampling jitter/alert-latency study, complete 5/15/30-minute offline trials, 20-cycle Wi-Fi recovery study or measured dashboard delay was available. This is why the testing objective is only partly achieved.

Reviewed report §§7.3.4, 7.5.1–7.5.5 · Recorded report results; synthetic AI figures are not clinical validation.

06 · Objectives 3 & 4 — Test and evaluate

Evidence, with clear limits.

Testing — partly achieved. Firmware build/upload, SD diagnostics and API checks passed; 21 backend tests passed. Reference accuracy, timing and controlled offline trials remain incomplete.

Evaluation — partly achieved. AI assessed on 480 synthetic sessions: 288 train / 96 validation / 96 test; 19,272 held-out rows.

AI row-level precision 0.9377 · recall 0.8177 · ROC-AUC 0.9748. These are simulation results, not clinical accuracy.

Specific objective 4 · Partly achieved

Evaluate performance against a baseline

Evaluate real-time performance, accuracy, alert timing and AI false-warning burden/lead time against threshold-only detection.

How we achieved it

  1. Generated 480 controlled synthetic sessions across eight scenarios. Split by session: 288 training, 96 validation and 96 test, keeping test sessions held out.
  2. Selected the logistic-regression decision threshold of 0.75 using validation data. Evaluated on 19,272 held-out synthetic rows.
  3. Counted row-level outcomes: 4,395 true positives, 13,605 true negatives, 292 false positives and 980 false negatives.
  4. Compared simulated event detection and warning burden with the threshold-only baseline, rather than claiming that a higher AI score proves clinical benefit.

Recorded evidence

93.77%Precision = 4,395 / (4,395 + 292)
81.77%Recall = 4,395 / (4,395 + 980)
44 / 49 vs 25 / 49Events detected at onset: AI versus threshold-only
107.5 s vs 0 sMedian simulated detection lead time

AI detected 19 more simulated events at onset. Event sensitivity increased from 51.0% to 89.8% (38.8 percentage points). ROC-AUC was 0.9748, a ranking measure—not “97.48% accuracy”.

Remaining work: False-warning episodes increased from 0.7472 to 1.4197 per simulated hour. Earlier detection therefore came with more warnings. Row-level false positives and warning episodes are different measures. Synthetic labels are not verified neonatal outcomes; reference accuracy, timing and clinical performance remain unestablished.

Reviewed report §§7.6.1–7.6.5 · Recorded report results; synthetic AI figures are not clinical validation.

07 · The human outcome

Earlier attention. Safer decisions.

NeoGuard does not replace nurses or doctors. It gives them a persistent local signal, preserved history and an explainable second layer of attention.

Our next step is calibrated reference testing, ethical clinical evaluation, power qualification and validation with real neonatal outcomes.

NeoGuard: sense locally · warn immediately · remember offline · explain trends · support care.
